home.title: Protect peaceful protest. Stop riot violence.
home.eyebrow: A petition to European and national decision-makers
home.headline: Protect the right to protest. Stop the violence that undermines it.
home.lead: Peaceful protest is a fundamental right in every European democracy. Arson, looting and attacks on people endanger residents, emergency workers and peaceful demonstrators alike. We ask for clear, lawful measures that stop the violent minority — so that everyone else can keep exercising their rights safely.
home.pointsIntro: Five proposals, each to be adopted through democratic processes and applied with full legal safeguards.

points.title: Protect peaceful protest
points.text: The freedom of peaceful assembly must be guaranteed and actively protected. Peaceful participants must never be treated as offenders because others turn violent.

points.title: Stop violence firmly
points.text: Arson, looting and attacks on people, police, emergency services or property must be stopped promptly and prosecuted consistently.

points.title: Military support as a last resort
points.text: When ordinary police resources are demonstrably overwhelmed, armed forces should be able to support civilian authorities — only under a clear legal framework, civilian command and parliamentary oversight.

points.title: Detention and return, after due process
points.text: People without legal residence who take part in serious violence should be held temporarily in simple, humane facilities and, after due process, prioritised for return — never in breach of the principle of non-refoulement.

points.title: A shared European entry ban
points.text: Strengthen a common European mechanism so that people convicted of serious public-order offences during riots can be refused entry across Europe, with individual assessment and judicial review.

home.goalText: Protect the right to protest by removing the violent minority from it.
home.ctaText: Every signature strengthens the call for a firm, lawful and rights-respecting response to riot violence.
home.shareTitle: Help the petition reach more people
home.shareText: Share the petition with friends, family and colleagues who care about safe streets and the right to protest.

share.messagesIntro: Feel free to copy, adapt or translate these.
messages: Peaceful protest is a right. Riot violence is not. I signed the European Public Order Initiative — will you?
Protect the right to protest by stopping the violent minority — within the rule of law and human rights. Sign here:
Arson, looting and attacks on people endanger everyone, including peaceful demonstrators. I support firm, lawful measures. Add your name:

facts.name: Name
facts.typeText: An independent, non-partisan citizens' petition. It is not a registered European Citizens' Initiative under Regulation (EU) 2019/788 and is not affiliated with the European Union or any of its institutions.
facts.addresseesText: The Members of the European Parliament, the European Commission, the Council of the European Union, and the governments and parliaments of the Member States of the European Union and the European Economic Area.

press.boilerplateIntro: Use these texts as they are, or shorten them as needed.
press.short: The European Public Order Initiative is an independent, non-partisan citizens' petition that calls for firm, lawful measures against riot violence in order to protect the right to peaceful protest.
press.long: The European Public Order Initiative is an independent, non-partisan citizens' petition addressed to European and national decision-makers. It asks for five measures: to protect peaceful protest; to stop arson, looting and attacks on people promptly and prosecute them consistently; to allow armed forces to support civilian authorities as a last resort, under civilian command and parliamentary oversight; to hold people without legal residence who take part in serious violence temporarily in humane facilities and, after due process, prioritise their return, never in breach of the principle of non-refoulement; and to strengthen a shared European entry ban for people convicted of serious public-order offences, with individual assessment and judicial review. Every measure must be adopted democratically and respect national constitutions, the European Convention on Human Rights and the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union. The petition is not affiliated with the European Union or any of its institutions.

rights.title: Our commitment to the rule of law
rights.text: This petition does not call for any illegal action. Every measure it proposes must be adopted through democratic, lawful processes and applied in full respect of national constitutions, the European Convention on Human Rights, the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union and international refugee law, including the principle of non-refoulement. Measures must target conduct — never nationality, ethnicity, religion or political opinion.
rights.short: This petition calls for no illegal action and fully respects national constitutions and the European Convention on Human Rights.
